liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Morning Dew** (2 other sources): Morning Dew is incomplete on this transfer; the track was not finished; The tape source never finished Morning Dew [2][3]
- **Hell in a Bucket** (1 review): Reviewer calls the opener a ripsnorter that starts the evening strongly [11]
- **Sugaree** (1 review): Reviewer lists Sugaree among the super hot first-set numbers, with Jerry's playing awesome [18]

## Setlist highlights

- **Fence Crashers Rap**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **Crowd Noise/Hard Days Night**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]

## The recordings

- **gd87-04-18.schoesp.eD.11659.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): source not stated; 21 songs; 154 min; rated 4.17/5 by 6 [1]
- **gd1987-04-18.senn441.corso.87639.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 22 songs; 148 min [2]
- **gd1987-04-18.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.83732.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 146 min; rated 3.56/5 by 9 [3]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says the recording sounds great, as expected from anything with Charlie Miller's name on it [18]
- **gd87-04-18.sbd.clugston.11882.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 18 songs; 148 min; rated 3.6/5 by 5 [8]

## Around the show

- Reviewer's tickets marked 'orch' meant the orchestra pit, not an orchard; he sat in the 17th row after the UIC shows [12]
- Local LA and Santa Cruz kids were irreverent, with talk of jumping the fence up in Lion Country at the start [12]
- An air show at El Toro Marine base and a jet crash clogged the freeway; jets swooped low over the parking lot and amphitheatre [13]
- Reviewer thinks someone in the Dead's sound crew sampled the jet sounds; he attended all three shows (Fri, Sat, Sun) [13]
- Reviewer corrects the aircraft: the Phantom was an F-4, and the jet seen was more likely a Harrier from El Toro [15]
- Reviewer finds this night opens stronger and the band tighter and more focused than the previous night, with a more even mix [11]
- Reviewer calls it an excellent late-'80s show capturing the energy building before the release of In the Dark [18]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd87-04-18.schoesp.eD.11659.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by DAT>CDR via Bad Man Brown; Seeded to etree by eD(efojr); source: Schoeps CMC 44Âs>DAT>CDR [1]. Also: Reviewer wanted patch material for the soundboard source and may use the board to patch this audience recording [16]
- **gd1987-04-18.senn441.corso.87639.sbeok.flac16**: taped by John Corso; transferred by Alex Ford; source: Sennheiser 441s > D5 > D5 > gold plated Monster Cables > D5 > Maxell XLII-S 90 (set I) TDK MA-R90 (set II) [2]. Also: Audience recording taped from the rail next to Healy, from master cassettes provided by Mark McCue; Set tape flips and the Fence Crashers Rap, Hard Days Night crowd noise were patched using another source (shnid 11659) [2]
- **gd1987-04-18.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.83732.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Maxell MX90/Sony D5) [3]. Also: Schoeps CMC4/MK4 mics to PCM, then DAT, then CD; tapes were labeled Broadcast Mix; tapes came from Paul Scotton and Joani Walker [3]
- **gd87-04-18.sbd.clugston.11882.sbeok.shnf**: source: Master Soundboard Casette > PCM> DAT> CDR EAC'ed/SHN'ed & Seeded to Etree by Scott Clugston [8]. Also: Disc 2 tracks run beyond 80 minutes, so the uploader put the second-set opener at the end of disc 1 [9]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Robbi Cohn: [1987-04-17 Irvine Meadows, Irvine, CA, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1987-04-17-irvine-meadows-irvine-ca-usa/) [22]
- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Irvine Meadows Amphitheatre - April 19, 1987](https://www.dead.net/show/april-19-1987) [23]
- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1987-04-18 Grateful Dead Backstage Pass - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1987-04-18-grateful-dead-backstage-pass/) [24]
